alex (docs): Heads-up — found multiple outdated code snippets in sample-app README that break auth and copy/paste security. Example: curl uses -H 'Api-Key: sk-live-...' and JS sample uses client.setApiKey('sk-...') instead of env var.

samir (sdk): ugh. thanks for flagging. we've had different header keys between Node and Python bindings (x-api-key vs Authorization). I'll audit parity.

maria (devex): also saw a literal sk- token in the README history (probably copy/paste). can we replace with process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY and add a warning about not pasting real keys? :warning:

linda (eng): let's add a simple regex check in pre-commit for sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{10,} and fail CI if found. do we have an existing linter hook? @ci-bot?

ci-bot: reproduced. sample-app/README.md line 54 contains "sk-live-xyz". failing test: docs/no-hardcoded-keys

alex (docs): i'll open a tiny PR to fix the examples, switch to Authorization: Bearer <env var>, and update the quickstart snippet. linking draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/pull/248

samir (sdk): thanks. also add a short unit test that loads the JS example and asserts it uses process.env. i can follow up to align Python snippet (requests with headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")}'})

alex (docs): here's the broken vs fixed curl snippet I plan to commit:
```bash
# broken
curl -H "Api-Key: sk-live-..." https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

# fixed
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

maria (devex): small DX ask: can we add a note in the README about SDK retry semantic differences? JS SDK retries idempotent requests only, python retries default all GET/POST — caused a bug with streaming. maybe add a cross-sdk parity table.

samir (sdk): good call. i'll add a checklist in the SDK repo: auth header, env var, retry behavior, example outputs. will open PR to SDK repo after docs PR merges. :+1:

alex (docs): PR merged (248) and backported to v1-quickstart branch. thanks everyone. closing the thread.
